name: NESTOR
full_name: Neutrino Extended Submarine Telescope with Oceanographic Research
summary: A historical Greek deep-sea telescope programme tested rigid star-shaped optical-detector floors off Pylos and contributed to the development of Mediterranean neutrino observatories.
detection_principle: Upward- and downward-facing photomultiplier pairs on titanium arms observed Cherenkov light. A shore-connected prototype floor demonstrated deep-water timing and muon reconstruction.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: Historical prototype operation is documented. A later paper describes future tower work; that is not evidence of a completed full array.

timeline.event: First shore-connected floor deployed in March.
Atmospheric-muon reconstruction from the prototype reported.
Design work fed into the broader KM3NeT effort; the original full tower was not established as an operating observatory.

collaboration.name: NESTOR Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Implemented prototype
key_parameters.value: One reduced-size detector floor deployed in 2003

key_parameters.name: Depth
key_parameters.value: Approximately 4,000 m in the Ionian Sea

key_parameters.name: Full tower design
key_parameters.value: 12 rigid floors with paired PMTs on six arms; proposed floor diameter approximately 32 m

results.summary: The prototype reconstructed the angular distribution of atmospheric muons in agreement with simulations, validating the basic deep-water readout concept.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
